components.name: Page skeleton
components.desc: The single HTML page every part of Pult lives in: the top bar, the text pane and the right-hand pane, plus the shared dialog and notice areas.
components.detail: index.html (about 6 KB) declares the PWA (manifest, icons, theme colour, no page zoom, notch-safe viewport) and links fonts.css and style.css. All behaviour comes from 20 classic `<script>` tags loaded in a fixed order into one global scope; there is no build step or module system. The markup is static: everything inside the panes is filled in later by the scripts.

mem: the bare DOM of the page, well under 1 MB
store: index.html, ~6 KB, kept in the app cache

components.name: Top bar
components.desc: One bar across the top with the menu, the title of the text, the marker, the Glosses / Grammar / Colours switches, the split and reading-mode buttons, the pane tabs and the search box.
components.detail: Static buttons with ids (`#btnMenu`, `#textTitle`, `#btnMark`, `#btnGlossToggle`, `#btnGram`, `#btnPos`, `#btnSplit`, `#btnRead`, `#tabEntry`, `#tabList`, `#tabMap`, `#search`) that app.js and the other scripts wire up. The ☰ menu lists Library, Export text, Instruments, Settings, This Pult and Acknowledgements. style.css keeps the bar to one row on wide screens and two rows on phones in portrait.

components.name: Two panes and the divider
components.desc: The text pane on the left (or top) and the dictionary pane on the right (or bottom), separated by a draggable divider.
components.detail: `#textPane` holds `#textBody`; `#dictPane` holds the dictionary entry (`#dictBody`), the lemma list (`#listBody`) and the map (`#mapBody`), only one shown at a time. `#divider` and the invisible `#edgeGrab` strip are the drag handles; the grid columns follow the CSS variable `--split`. In portrait the grid turns into rows.

components.name: Dialog, notices and floating buttons
components.desc: Shared places for pop-ups: one modal dialog, the short notice ("toast"), the floating +Gloss / +Default / highlight buttons and hidden file pickers.
components.detail: Every dialog in Pult reuses the single `<dialog id="dlg">` with its form `#dlgForm`. `#toast` is moved into an open dialog when needed (see `toast`). `#fabBar` appears over a text selection in the dictionary; `#fileDict`, `#fileText` and `#fileBackup` are invisible file inputs opened from menus.

components.name: Script load order
components.desc: The order in which the program files are loaded, which decides what each file can use while it loads.
components.detail: core.js, analysis.js, text.js, dictview.js, dialogs.js, export.js, library.js, libtime.js, libmenu.js, librev.js, glosses.js, search.js, app.js, then the map scripts maps.js … mapsun.js. Code that runs during loading may only use what earlier scripts defined; `main` in app.js therefore waits for DOMContentLoaded so that the map scripts have run. Large libraries (three.js, MapLibre) are not in this list; the map code loads them on demand.

mem: the parsed JavaScript of all scripts, est. a few MB
cpu: parsing ~0.9 MB of JavaScript at start-up

components.name: Start-up
components.desc: What happens when Pult opens: the storage is opened, your settings are restored, the dictionaries are registered and the last text reopens.
components.detail: Implemented by the anonymous `main` function at the end of app.js. It runs once per page load, awaits each step in turn and then schedules a few background jobs. Nothing here needs the network; only the scheduled update check goes online.
components.netNote: works offline; the update check it schedules needs the network

mem: settings and the dictionary list, plus whatever the reopened text needs
cpu: one burst at load, mostly waiting for IndexedDB

components.name: Start-up sequence
components.desc: Opens the database, restores every saved preference and reopens the text you were reading.
components.detail: Registers the service worker (`sw.js`, not on file://), waits for DOMContentLoaded, then `openDB`, `migrateOld` and `wire`. It restores theme, fades, notices, gloss mode, Latin vowel lengths, default glosses (`lg|…` settings), gloss/grammar switches, map on/off, split, text size, source colours, word-class colours and the grammar-line choice, then calls `loadDicts`, the search settings and `openText` for `currentText`. Without any dictionaries it shows a welcome with a button that downloads the free set (`syncPackages`). Finally it asks the browser for persistent storage (`navigator.storage.persist`).

mem: the settings rows, the lemma→default-gloss map (S.lemmaGloss), est. < 5 MB

components.name: Delayed background jobs
components.desc: Tasks that start a little after opening so they do not slow the start: looking for package updates, tidying storage, upgrading old glosses.
components.detail: Scheduled from `main` with timers: `updCheck` after 5 s (only when `navigator.onLine`), `housekeep` after 20 s and `glossMigrate` after 30 s; errors are swallowed. The jobs themselves live in dialogs.js and glosses.js.
components.netNote: the update check runs only when online; the other two are offline

cpu: only the timers here; the work is in the called jobs

components.name: Core helpers and shared state
components.desc: Small building blocks used by every other part: page helpers, Greek/Latin word keys, notices and the one shared state object.
components.detail: core.js is loaded first, so everything else can rely on it. It defines no UI of its own apart from the notice and the iPad Pencil fix. All later scripts read and write the global state object `S` directly.

mem: the helpers themselves are tiny; S is counted in its own node
cpu: called constantly but each call is cheap

components.name: Page helpers
components.desc: Two one-line helpers used everywhere: find an element and make text safe for HTML.
components.detail: `$` is `document.querySelector`; `esc` escapes &, <, > and " before text is placed into HTML strings. Most of Pult builds its UI as HTML strings, so `esc` is what keeps imported texts and glosses from being read as markup.

cpu: cheap, but called for every word drawn

components.name: Greek and Latin word keys
components.desc: Recognises Greek and Latin words in a text and turns them into the keys used to look them up.
components.detail: `WORD_TOKEN` (built from `GREEK_TOKEN` and `LATIN_TOKEN`) finds words, including a trailing elision mark; `isGreek` / `langOf` decide the language by alphabet. `canon` gives the exact form (grave → acute, circumflex unified, elision mark unified, lower case); `gkey` drops all accents and breathings and folds final sigma; `latkey` drops diacritics and folds j→i, v→u, æ→ae. `stripSecondAccent` removes the extra accent an enclitic throws back (αἴτιός → αἴτιος) so such forms can still be found. Packages built by the greekdict toolkit use the same keys.

cpu: Unicode normalisation per word; many calls when a long text is analysed

components.name: Short notices
components.desc: The brief messages that appear and fade, e.g. "Gloss saved" or "Marker moved here".
components.detail: `toast` shows a message for 2.5 s by default: at the bottom, higher up, or just above a given element (used for the map time slider), kept inside the window and placed inside an open dialog if there is one. It fades in over 1/9 s and out over 1/3 s unless Fades are off (`body.nofade`). `note` is the quiet variant for confirmations: it only shows when Settings → Appearance → Notices is on.

components.name: Shared state (S)
components.desc: The memory of the running app: the open text and its words, glosses, installed dictionaries, the dictionary view, and many UI flags.
components.detail: `S` is a single global object that every script reads and extends (e.g. `S.text`, `S.tokens`, `S.glosses`, `S.cur`, `S.view`, `S.dicts`, `S.morph`, `S.posCfg`, `S.gramCfg`, `S.lemmaGloss`, `S.TW`). Nothing in it is saved automatically; whatever must survive is written to IndexedDB by the code that changes it. Its size is dominated by `S.tokens`: one object per word and punctuation run of the open text, later enriched with lemma, analysis, word class and grammar text.

mem: est. 5-30 MB for a long book (one token object per word with lemma/analysis/grammar strings), plus the Latin engine when loaded

components.name: iPad Pencil fix
components.desc: Stops the Apple Pencil handwriting feature (Scribble) from swallowing taps on buttons that sit next to text fields.
components.detail: Only on iPads (`IS_IPAD`): every text field is made read-only while not in use and unlocked on pointerdown, touchstart or focus, then locked again on leaving. A MutationObserver locks fields in any newly added content, so dialogs built later are covered too.

cpu: a querySelectorAll on each DOM insertion, iPad only

components.name: Database access
components.desc: Pult's doorway to on-device storage: opens the main database and the per-dictionary databases and offers simple read/write helpers.
components.detail: Everything you create (texts, glosses, choices, settings) goes into IndexedDB 'greekreader'; each dictionary has its own database 'greekreader-dict-<id>' so deleting one gives the space back. The helpers wrap IndexedDB requests in promises; there is no caching layer on top.

store: the main database is small (texts, glosses, settings: est. KB to a few MB); dictionaries are counted under packages

components.name: Main database
components.desc: Opens IndexedDB 'greekreader' with its five stores.
components.detail: `openDB` creates (version 1) the stores `dicts` (installed packages), `texts` (auto-increment, imported texts), `glosses` (auto-increment, indexed by `textId`), `choices` (lemma chosen for a form, key `f`) and `settings` (key/value, key `k`). The open connection is kept in the global `db`.

store: texts + glosses + settings, est. < 10 MB for typical use

components.name: Read/write helpers
components.desc: Short promise-based helpers for reading and writing records.
components.detail: `tx` opens a transaction on the main database; `req2p` and `done` turn a request or a transaction into a promise; `get`, `getAll`, `put` and `del` do one operation each in their own transaction. Bulk writes use `bulkPut` (in analysis.js) instead.

components.name: Settings store
components.desc: Saves and reads every preference and small per-text value.
components.detail: `setting(k)` reads and `setting(k, v)` writes a row of the `settings` store. Besides plain preferences (theme, split, textZoom, posCfg, gramCfg, dictPrefs …) it holds prefixed keys: `lg|<lemma>` default glosses, `mk|<text>` markers, `pos|`/`pw|<text>` reading positions, `an|<text>|<word>` the reading chosen for a word, `wk|`, `opened`, `currentText`.

store: settings store, est. KB to ~1 MB (grows with default glosses and word choices)

components.name: Dictionary databases
components.desc: Opens, closes and deletes the separate database of each installed dictionary.
components.detail: `dictDB(id)` opens 'greekreader-dict-<id>' (one store `b`: key-prefix buckets) and keeps the connection promise in `dictConns`; a version change closes it. `dropDictDB` closes the connection and deletes the whole database. `listDBs` lists databases where the browser supports it.

store: code only (the data is counted under packages)

components.name: One-time storage move
components.desc: Moves data from the old single database 'greekdict' into the current layout, once.
components.detail: `migrateOld` checks for the old database; if found, it shows a progress dialog, copies texts, glosses, choices, settings and dictionaries, and copies each dictionary's buckets 200 rows at a time into its own database. Afterwards the old database is deleted. On current installs it returns at once.

mem: 200 rows at a time while migrating
cpu: usually none; heavy only during the one-time move

components.name: Taps, menus and live settings
components.desc: Connects the page to the code: what happens when you tap a word, a menu item, a switch in Settings or pick a file.
components.detail: Almost all of it is set up by one large function, `wire` (about 23 KB), called once at start-up. It mostly uses event delegation on `document` and on the panes, then hands over to functions in the other scripts. The children below describe its main groups; they are all parts of `wire`.

components.name: Listener set-up (wire)
components.desc: Registers every global listener once when Pult starts.
components.detail: `wire` attaches about 80 listeners: clicks, changes and inputs on the text pane, dictionary pane and lemma list, document-wide delegated handlers for dialogs, pointer and selection events, the divider drag and the scroll and visibility handlers that save the reading position (`saveReadPos`). It also calls the wiring functions of other scripts (`wireMarker`, `wireReading`, `wireSearch`, `wireLibrary`, `wireRevisions`, `wirePencilSelect`, `wireTouchSelect` on Android, `wireDictScroll`, `wireDictDrag`).

cpu: once at start-up; scroll handlers are throttled (rAF / 500 ms)

components.name: Taps in the panes
components.desc: Tapping a word in the text looks it up; tapping in the dictionary chooses a lemma or reading; tapping a lemma in the list jumps to the word.
components.detail: A word tap sets the selection `S.cur` and calls `showWord`; a tap on a gloss opens its gloss field (`openGlossField`); tapping empty space hides the selection. In the dictionary pane, lemma chips and analyses call `setTokChoice`, the ★ pin stores a lemma for the form in `choices`, and Greek words inside entries are looked up in turn. In the lemma list, sort/filter buttons re-render it and a row scrolls the text to its word (`ensureWord`). While an export range is being picked, word taps only set its start and end.

components.name: Menu and top-bar actions
components.desc: Opens the right dialog from the ☰ menu, the title, the tabs and long presses on the top-bar buttons.
components.detail: The ☰ menu maps its items to `libraryDialog`, `exportDialog`, `dictsDialog` (Instruments), `settingsDialog`, `pultDialog` and `acksDialog`; the title opens `navDialog`. The Dictionary and Lemmata tabs switch the right pane (`showTab`) and restore its scroll position. Holding Grammar opens Settings → Grammar line, holding Colours (550 ms) opens the word-class colours; long presses on items with `data-tip` show their tip as a notice.

components.name: Settings that act at once
components.desc: Changes made in Settings and Instruments take effect immediately, without a Save button.
components.detail: Delegated change/click handlers apply theme, gloss mode, Latin vowel lengths, colours on/off, grammar line, source colours and dictionary on/off (which reloads the dictionary list, clears the bucket cache and re-analyses the text when a morphology tool is switched). Word-class buttons toggle grammar-line and colour classes; holding a colour chip opens an 18-colour palette with "Other …" for the system picker. Each change is saved with `setting`.

cpu: per change; switching a morphology tool re-analyses the open text

components.name: File pickers
components.desc: Reads files you pick: dictionary packages, backups and texts to import.
components.detail: `#fileDict` hands packages to `importFiles`, `#fileBackup` to `restoreBackup`; `#fileText` and the import dialog accept plain text or Pult JSON (`greekdict-text-1`, `greekdict-backup-1`) and pass it to `saveText` or the import form (`readTextFile` for other text files).

mem: the picked file while it is read

components.name: Selection and the floating buttons
components.desc: When you select text in a dictionary entry, buttons appear to add it as a gloss, as the default gloss, or to highlight it.
components.detail: A debounced (60 ms) `selectionchange` handler asks `dictSelection` what is selected and shows the bar with `updateFab`. + Gloss and + Default call `addGloss(text, asDefault, true)`, which appends to an existing gloss; the highlighter calls `toggleHighlight`. The buttons cancel pointerdown so the selection is not lost.

components.name: Split between the panes
components.desc: How much room the text and the dictionary get, from dictionary only to text only.
components.detail: The split is a CSS variable `--split` on the root element, saved as the setting `split`. The split button bounces through fixed steps, dragging the divider sets any value, and the reading position is kept while the panes resize.

cpu: a full relayout of both panes on each change; continuous while dragging

components.name: Split value and button
components.desc: Sets the split and cycles it with the split button.
components.detail: `setSplit` writes `--split`, switches `solo-dict` / `solo-text` at the extremes (the hidden pane keeps its size in `--tw` / `--dw` so lines do not re-wrap), updates the icon and the gloss width and saves the value. `cycleSplit` steps 0 → 1/3 → 1/2 → 2/3 → 1 and back (`SPLITS`), restoring the text anchor afterwards; `getSplit` reads the current value (also used by the map).

components.name: Split icon
components.desc: Draws the split button as an open book whose fold sits where the split is.
components.detail: `splitIcon` generates an SVG: page edges and four text lines as quadratic Bézier curves sloping toward the fold, rotated 90° in portrait; its title says "Text 1/3", "Dictionary only" and so on. It is redrawn on every split change and orientation change.

components.name: Divider drag and solo panes
components.desc: Drag the divider to resize the panes; pull it to an edge to read or look up full-width.
components.detail: Part of `wire`: a pointer drag on `#divider` or `#edgeGrab` maps the pointer to a percentage (clamped to 15–85 %, under 7 % → dictionary only, over 93 % → text only), calls `setSplit` without saving on each move and keeps the text anchor; the value is saved on release. The invisible edge strip lets you pull a hidden pane back.

cpu: relayout of both panes on every pointer move while dragging

components.name: Top-bar switches and theme
components.desc: The on/off switches for glosses and the grammar line, light/dark theme, and the search box that adapts to its width.
components.detail: Each switch toggles a class on `<body>` (`nogloss`, `gram`) or an attribute on `<html>` (`data-theme`), which style.css reacts to, and saves its state.

cpu: per switch; a class change relayouts the text

components.name: Glosses switch
components.desc: Shows or hides all interlinear glosses.
components.detail: `setGlossVisible` toggles `body.nogloss`, the button state and the setting `showGloss`.

components.name: Grammar switch
components.desc: Shows or hides the grammatical information line under each word.
components.detail: `setGram` toggles `body.gram`, the button and the setting `showGram`; `applyTopButtons` keeps the Grammar button visible (it is always shown now).

components.name: Light and dark theme
components.desc: Switches between the light (paper) and dark look; dark is the default.
components.detail: `setTheme` sets `data-theme` on `<html>` (style.css swaps its colour variables), changes the browser's theme colour and, if the map is open, rebuilds the map style with `mapStyle(mapColors())` and refreshes its data.

cpu: restyle of the page; a map style rebuild if the map is open

components.name: Search box fitting
components.desc: When the search box is too narrow for "Look up a word…", a magnifying glass replaces the placeholder.
components.detail: Part of `wire`: a ResizeObserver measures the placeholder with a canvas 2D context and toggles the class `phicon`; a `filled` class marks a non-empty box because Safari treats an empty placeholder differently.

components.name: Stylesheet
components.desc: All of the look of Pult: colours, layout, the top bar, panes, dialogs, Library, map controls and animations.
components.detail: One hand-written file, style.css (~229 KB, ~2,000 lines, ~70 media queries). About 70 KB of it are photos embedded as base64 (the Dictionary and Lemmata tab pictures and the map icon). Colours are CSS variables on `:root`, redefined for `[data-theme=dark]`; text size is scaled by `--tz` and the split by `--split`. Two small rule sets are generated at run time instead (`#posStyle`, `#gramStyle`).

mem: the parsed style rules and decoded tab/map pictures, est. 1-3 MB
store: style.css, ~229 KB in the app cache
cpu: style recalculation on class changes; parsed once

components.name: Base, colours and top bar
components.desc: The colour palette for light and dark, the basic page grid, the divider, the top bar and its responsive variants.
components.detail: About 18 KB: theme variables (`--bg`, `--fg`, `--acc`, `--gloss` …, fonts `--greek` and `--ui`), the panes grid and the divider's grab zone, scroll-bar colours, and the top bar for desktop, portrait (two rows), phones in landscape and small phones.

components.name: Text and dictionary styles
components.desc: How the text with its glosses and grammar line looks, and how dictionary entries and the lemma list are laid out.
components.detail: About 19 KB: each word as an inline column (word, grammar line, gloss), selection and highlight colours, verse references in the margin, the reading mode, solo panes, the text's scroll handle and the part boxes of long texts; dictionary entries, Latin sense paragraphs, the back/forward pill and the narrow-pane variants.

cpu: text layout of every drawn word

components.name: Dialogs, Settings, Instruments, search, export
components.desc: The look of the shared dialog: Settings and Instruments menus, folded sections, switches, colour chips, the search suggestions and results, and the export options.
components.detail: About 36 KB: the sticky dialog title with ✕, two-level menus, joined switches, word-class chips and the colour palette, the This Pult and gloss-review pages, search suggestions and results page, and export range picking and print layout.

components.name: Library styles
components.desc: The look of the Library and text navigation: tabs, rows of authors and works, filters, the date line, downloads and revisions.
components.detail: About 43 KB, the largest plain section: Library tabs and rows, the work page, the navigation outline and title on narrow screens, filter sheets for phones, the century slider and period line, the download icon that fills like a vessel, and the revisions list.

components.name: Map controls styles
components.desc: The look of everything around the map: buttons, menus, time slider, drawing bar, sundial panel, the owl and the obelisk.
components.detail: About 53 KB, including a 16.6 KB base64 picture for the map button (Natural Earth II). Covers place marks in the text, the layers menu, time slider, selection cards, drawing tools, relief labels, imagery credits, Globe menu, relief saving, sundial panel and owl animation.

mem: small, plus the decoded map icon
gpu: a few CSS animations (owl) when shown

components.name: Tab pictures
components.desc: The photos on the Dictionary and Lemmata tabs (Pape's Handwörterbuch and index cards), in colour and grey.
components.detail: About 55 KB of base64 JPEGs in CSS variables (`--pape`, `--papeg`, `--cards`, `--cardsg`), with separate grey versions for the dark theme; the coloured picture fades in over the grey one when a tab is selected.

components.name: Fades
components.desc: Short colour and opacity transitions on buttons, tabs and notices, switchable in Settings → Appearance → Fades.
components.detail: About 4 KB: buttons take their accent colour over 1/9 s and lose it over 1/3 s, tab pictures and top-bar switches fade, notices fade in and out. All of it is disabled when `body.nofade` is set.

components.name: Fonts
components.desc: The typefaces: Gentium Book Plus for Greek and Latin text, Source Sans 3 for the interface, Roboto Condensed for the grammar line.
components.detail: fonts.css (~6 KB) declares 19 `@font-face` rules pointing at woff2 files in fonts/ (about 670 KB in all, SIL OFL); all use `font-display: swap`, so text shows at once in a fallback face. The files are part of the app and are cached for offline use like the other app files.

mem: decoded font faces in use, est. 1-3 MB
store: font files ~670 KB in the app cache

components.name: Gentium Book Plus (text)
components.desc: The reading face for Greek and Latin, in regular, bold and italic.
components.detail: Sixteen faces: Greek, Greek Extended, Latin and Latin Extended subsets for 400 normal, 700 normal, 400 italic and (since v348) 700 italic (`--greek` in style.css). These rules have no `unicode-range`, so a browser may fetch several subsets of a style even for one script (est.).

components.name: Source Sans 3 (interface)
components.desc: The face of buttons, menus, glosses and dialogs.
components.detail: A variable font (weights 200–900) in six subset files (Greek, Greek Extended, Latin, Latin Extended; normal and italic Latin), each limited by `unicode-range` so only the needed subsets are fetched; used as `--ui`.

components.name: Roboto Condensed (grammar line)
components.desc: A narrow face for the small grammar line under each word, so "masc/neut gen sg" fits.
components.detail: One Latin-only file (~21 KB) with a `unicode-range` for basic Latin.

components.name: Opening a text and keeping your place
components.desc: Loads a text or library book, splits it into words, and keeps the reading position and your bookmark.
components.detail: Everything starts with `openText`, which fills `S.text`, `S.tokens` and `S.glosses`, draws the text and starts the word analysis. Because iOS tends to jump to the top when the text is redrawn or the keyboard opens, an anchor (a word and its distance from the top) is remembered and restored around every redraw.

mem: the text and its tokens, est. 1-30 MB for a long book
store: reads texts/glosses/settings from the main database

components.name: Open a text
components.desc: Opens an imported text or a book from the Library, with its glosses, marker and saved position.
components.detail: `openText(id)` saves the old position, loads the text (`loadBook` for library books, else the `texts` store), tokenises it, applies a GLAUx annotation if the book has one (`applyAnnotation`), builds the reference list (`refsOf`), loads the marker, records when it was opened, updates the title bar, reads the glosses by `textId` and the per-word reading choices, draws the text, restores the scroll position or anchor (`pos|` / `pw|` settings) and finally starts `resolveTokens`. It is called from the Library, navigation, search, maps and start-up.

mem: the whole text string and its token array, est. up to tens of MB for the longest books
store: reads texts, glosses and several settings

components.name: Splitting into words
components.desc: Breaks a text into words, punctuation and (for library books) blocks and references.
components.detail: `tokenize` normalises to NFC and uses `WORD_TOKEN` to produce word tokens `{t:"w", s, i}` numbered in reading order and punctuation runs `{t:"p"}`. `tokenizeBlocks` does the same for library books stored as blocks `[kind, [[ref, text] …]]`, adding block (`b`) and reference (`r`) tokens; verse blocks mark their references as line numbers. Search, glosses, maps and revisions call the same functions so word numbers match everywhere.

mem: one small object per word and gap
cpu: a regex pass over the text, once per open

components.name: Keeping the reading position
components.desc: Keeps the line you are reading in place when the text is redrawn, the panes are resized or the keyboard opens.
components.detail: `textAnchor` records the selected word (or the first word at the top) and its offset; `applyTextAnchor` scrolls it back, drawing its part first in long texts (`ensureWord`). `guardText` re-applies the anchor several times within a second (rAF, 120 ms, 400 ms …) unless the user starts scrolling; the visual-viewport resize handler uses the same guard.

cpu: a few layout reads per redraw

components.name: Marker (bookmark)
components.desc: One ribbon bookmark per text: tap to set or jump to it, hold to move it here.
components.detail: `wireMarker` handles the top-bar ribbon: a tap sets the marker at the selected or first visible word (`anchorWord`, a binary search over the drawn words) or jumps to it (`goMarker`, with a short flash); a 550 ms hold moves it, or removes it when held at the same place. `setMarker` saves it as `mk|<text>`; `renderMarker` and `markIcon` draw the ribbon in the text and update the button.

components.name: Drawing the text
components.desc: Turns the words into the interactive text: each word with its grammar line and gloss beneath, coloured by word class; long books are drawn only near the screen.
components.detail: Texts up to 2,500 words are drawn whole; longer ones are cut into parts of about 200 words that are drawn when they come within three screens and emptied again beyond six (`S.TW`). Drawing builds HTML strings (`textHTML`) and sets `innerHTML`; word elements are kept in `S.wordEls` by word number so later updates need no selectors.

mem: DOM of the drawn words (4 elements per word); windowing caps this for long books, est. 5-40 MB
cpu: HTML build + layout on open, on every redraw and while scrolling long books

components.name: Word HTML
components.desc: Builds the markup of each word with its grammar line and glosses, and of the punctuation and references between words.
components.detail: `textHTML(n0, n1, …)` writes block and paragraph divs, margin references (verse numbers every 5th line), and per word a `.w` span with the word (or its Latin form with vowel lengths), the grammar line `.gm` and the glosses `.gl`; punctuation right after a word is glued to it. `glossMaps` indexes the glosses by first word and records which words are covered; `punctHTML` wraps punctuation so it can be coloured.

mem: the HTML string of the part being drawn
cpu: string building for every drawn word

components.name: Draw and redraw
components.desc: Draws the open text into the pane (whole or windowed) and highlights the selected word.
components.detail: `renderText` keeps the anchor when the same text is redrawn, chooses whole or windowed drawing (`LONG_TEXT` = 2,500 words), adds the next/previous book buttons, marks places (`markPlaces`), restores the position and refreshes the gloss box. `markTarget` highlights the selected word or range; `drawnWords` lists the drawn word elements; `textRoot` builds a full copy of the text for exports when only parts are on the page.

mem: whole-text DOM for short texts; for exports a full off-screen copy (est. tens of MB for a long book)
cpu: a full redraw after saving a gloss, choosing a reading or changing a setting

components.name: Parts of long texts
components.desc: Cuts a long book into parts of about 200 words, beginning at section breaks, and sets them up as empty boxes.
components.detail: `textChunks` starts a new part at a block once the current one has `CHUNK_W` (200) words; a text without breaks, or with one very long section, is drawn whole instead. `textWindowStart` writes placeholder divs of measured or estimated height and an IntersectionObserver with a 300 % margin that draws parts as they approach.

components.name: Drawing parts on demand
components.desc: Draws a part of a long text when it comes near the screen, without making the text jump.
components.detail: `chDraw` fills a part with `textHTML`, registers its words, and if the part is above the screen corrects the scroll position by the change in height; it also updates the average height per word used for estimates. `chDecorate` re-applies the selection, export range and place marks to a freshly drawn part; `ensureWord` draws the part containing a word before a jump.

cpu: layout of ~200 words per part while scrolling

components.name: Emptying far parts
components.desc: Removes parts that are far from the screen to keep memory low.
components.detail: 400 ms after scrolling stops, `chSweep` empties every drawn part more than six screens away; `chErase` stores its height, clears its word references and leaves an empty box of the same height.

components.name: Height estimates
components.desc: Keeps the empty parts at the right height when text size, width, glosses or grammar line change.
components.detail: `chKey` describes the layout (text size, width, body classes); a height measured under another key is not reused. `chEst` returns the measured height or words × average height per word. `chReestimate`, triggered 250 ms after a resize or class change, re-measures the drawn parts and resizes the empty ones, shifting the scroll position for those above the screen.

cpu: reads every part's height after a layout change

components.name: Interlinear glosses
components.desc: Your own translations written under words or phrases, plus a default gloss per lemma used everywhere it appears.
components.detail: A gloss belongs to a span of words in one text (`glosses` store); a default gloss belongs to a lemma (`lg|<lemma>` in settings) and is shown wherever that lemma occurs, either only where there is no own gloss or always (gloss mode "both"). Glosses are edited in the gloss box at the top of the dictionary pane or added from a selection in a dictionary entry.

store: glosses store + lg| settings, est. KB to a few MB
cpu: saving a gloss redraws the text

components.name: Saving glosses
components.desc: Creates, changes and deletes glosses and default glosses.
components.detail: `saveSpanGloss` creates, updates or (for empty text) deletes the gloss of a word or phrase, stamping it with its words and context via `glossStamp` so it can be re-attached after a text revision. `setDefaultGloss` sets or removes a lemma's default gloss; `cleanGloss` tidies spaces but keeps typed line breaks; `joinGloss` appends with "; " unless already present; `spanGloss` finds a gloss; `targetLemma` gives the lemma of the selected word as chosen in the dictionary pane.

components.name: Adding glosses
components.desc: Adds selected dictionary text as a gloss or a default gloss.
components.detail: `addGloss(text, asDefault, add)` checks that a text and word (or a lemma) is selected, appends or replaces, records the lemma name (`lemmaNameSet`) for default glosses, redraws and confirms with a notice. `writeGloss` and `editGloss` are older dialog-based editors that nothing in the current code calls.

components.name: Gloss box
components.desc: The two editable fields at the top of the dictionary pane: the gloss of the tapped word or phrase and the default gloss of its lemma.
components.detail: `fillGlossBox` writes the two textareas for the current selection and lemma, but leaves them alone while one is being edited; `autoGrow` sizes them to their content. `openGlossField` makes sure the word is shown in the dictionary pane (`showWord`) and puts the cursor at the end of the requested field. Saving happens on change in `wire` (Enter finishes, Shift+Enter adds a line).

components.name: Gloss display
components.desc: How glosses appear under the words: blue, small, wider when long, never wider than the text column.
components.detail: `glossHTML` escapes a gloss and keeps its line breaks; `dgHTML` renders a lemma's default gloss; `glW` widens a gloss longer than 70 characters in proportion (`--gw`), and `setGlossMax` caps it at 80 % of the text width (`--glmax`), re-run by a ResizeObserver on the text body.

components.name: Text size and touch gestures
components.desc: Pinch the text (or ctrl + wheel) to make it larger or smaller without zooming the whole page, and drag a wide scroll handle on touch screens.
components.detail: The size is one CSS variable `--tz` on `#textBody` (60–250 %), so text, glosses and grammar line scale together, and the word under the fingers stays in place. It is saved as `textZoom`, 400 ms after the gesture ends.

cpu: a relayout of the text every animation frame while pinching

components.name: Setting the text size
components.desc: Applies a new text size and keeps the reading position.
components.detail: `setTextZoom(z, at)` clamps and rounds the factor, sets `--tz`, then keeps either the word under the pinch point or the anchor at the top in place; it updates the gloss width, schedules a height re-estimate for long texts and the percentage shown in Settings. `tzSave` saves the value with a 400 ms debounce (`tzSaveT`); `TZ_MIN` (with `TZ_MAX`) bounds the range.

components.name: Pinch, wheel and scroll handle
components.desc: Recognises pinches and ctrl-wheel on the text, blocks page zoom elsewhere, and provides a finger-sized scroll handle.
components.detail: text.js's top-level code: two-finger touch pinches (scaled to the 0.75th power, throttled to one `setTextZoom` per frame), Safari `gesture*` events, ctrl + wheel (7 % per mouse notch, smooth for trackpads) and the Settings size buttons (`data-tz`); the map and the time slider keep their own pinch. On coarse pointers it adds `#tScroll`, a 34 px wide handle that appears while scrolling, fades after 1.4 s and can be dragged. It also installs the ResizeObserver and class MutationObserver that trigger `chReestimate` (`window.chLater`).

components.name: Choosing the reading of each word
components.desc: Works out for every word of the open text its lemma, its grammatical reading, its word class and the text of its grammar line.
components.detail: After a text opens, `resolveTokens` goes through all words in the background, using your own choices first, then a choice for the form, then the annotation of the passage (GLAUx), then the most likely lemma. Results are written onto the token objects and straight into the drawn word elements, so the text fills in progressively.

mem: memoised analyses and prefetched morphology buckets for the whole run, est. 10-100+ MB for very long books
cpu: analysis of every word once per text open (long books: seconds)

components.name: Analysing the whole text
components.desc: Fills in lemma, reading, word class and grammar line for every word, updating the text as it goes.
components.detail: `resolveTokens` numbers each run so a newer run cancels an older one; `resolveTokens1` reads all `choices` once, prefetches the Greek morphology buckets needed by the next 1,500 words in one transaction, memoises analyses per form, and for each word sets `lemma`, `ana`, `pos`, Latin vowel lengths (`q`) and `gram`, patching the class, grammar line and default gloss of its drawn element. At the end it redraws if needed and starts place detection (`placesForText`) and lemma names (`lemmaNamesFill`). `resetTokens` clears results so words are re-analysed; `classifyTokens` is an old alias.

mem: the bucket map and memo grow for the whole run; est. tens of MB for long books
cpu: once per open; per-word work is light but long books have 100k+ words

components.name: Readings from the annotation (GLAUx)
components.desc: For library books with a treebank annotation, uses the reading that the context suggests for each word.
components.detail: `applyAnnotation` attaches the annotation (lemma index + 9-position tag) to each word, but only if the word count matches exactly. `ctxReading` takes the lemma of the annotation (if the morphology knows it, `lemKey`) and picks the analysis that best fits the tag; `tagScore` compares an analysis such as "pres ind act 3rd sg" with the tag positions via `TAGF` / `TAGCAT`.

mem: one small context object per word
cpu: scores every candidate analysis per annotated word

components.name: Picking one reading
components.desc: Decides which lemma and which analysis a word shows.
components.detail: `pickReading` applies the order: your choice for this very word > your ★ choice for the form > the annotation's reading > the most likely lemma with its first analysis. It also reports whether the word is ambiguous (differing grammar lines, shown in a different style) and whether the shown reading was set by you.

components.name: Your reading for a word
components.desc: Remembers which lemma and analysis you chose for one particular word of a text.
components.detail: `setTokChoice` saves or removes `an|<text>|<word>` in settings, re-analyses that word, redraws the text and refreshes the dictionary view; `loadTokCh` loads all choices of a text into `S.tokCh` when it opens.

components.name: Morphology and dictionary lookup
components.desc: Finds the possible lemmas and grammatical analyses of a Greek or Latin form, and the dictionary entries for a key.
components.detail: Greek forms are looked up in the installed morphology package (a big form → analyses table split into buckets); Latin forms are analysed by a small engine that combines stems and endings (Collatinus or Whitaker's Words data). Dictionary and morphology data are read bucket by bucket from IndexedDB with a 300-bucket memory cache.

mem: bucket cache (≤300 buckets, ~10 KB each in JSON, est. 3-10 MB) plus the Latin engine (est. 20-40 MB when loaded)
cpu: per lookup; Latin analysis is pure computation

components.name: Greek analysis
components.desc: Lists the lemmas and analyses of a Greek form and which lemma is preferred.
components.detail: `analyses(form)` canonicalises the form, finds it in its morphology bucket (also without a second enclitic accent), groups the analyses by lemma and picks a lemma: your ★ choice, else the package's or the hints' preference (`morphPref`), else the first. Latin forms are passed on to `latAnalyses`. It is used by the dictionary, search, glosses, Library and maps as well.

components.name: Latin analysis engine
components.desc: Analyses Latin forms by splitting them into stem and ending, as Collatinus or Whitaker's Words do.
components.detail: `latEngine` loads the installed engine (the single `engine` record of the chosen package) once into memory and derives Latin word classes (`S.latPos`). `latAnalyze` tries every stem/ending split (`latAnalyzeKeyC` for Collatinus, `wwAnalyzeKey` + `wwFits` for Whitaker), plus contracted perfects, assimilated prefixes (adc-/acc-) and the enclitics -que/-ne/-ve. `latAnalyses` groups the results by lemma and puts the most frequent lemma first (`latFreq`).

mem: the whole engine as one object: Collatinus ~7.6 MB / Whitaker ~2.7 MB of JSON, est. 20-40 MB in memory
cpu: loading the engine once; then string work per form

components.name: Latin vowel lengths
components.desc: Puts macrons and breves on Latin words (rŏsā) when "vowel lengths" is on.
components.detail: `quantify` transfers the marks of the analysed spelling onto the form as written, keeping its case and i/j, u/v, or gives up if the letters do not match; `qCommon` keeps only the marks all readings agree on. Whitaker's data has no lengths, so `colEngine` loads the Collatinus engine as well and `qFromCol` takes the lengths of the closest Collatinus analysis of the same lemma (`QTOK`, `CONS`).

mem: a second Latin engine when Whitaker is used, est. 20 MB

components.name: Bucket reading and cache
components.desc: Fetches the piece ("bucket") of a dictionary or morphology database that holds a given key.
components.detail: `bucketOf` maps a key to its bucket name exactly like the toolkit's `bucket_of()` (a 3-letter prefix, longer where a prefix was split). `bucket` reads it from the dictionary's database and keeps it in `bucketCache`, a Map that drops the oldest entry beyond 300.

mem: up to 300 buckets (~10-12 KB JSON each on average, some > 100 KB), est. 3-10 MB

components.name: Finding dictionary entries
components.desc: Gives the dictionary pane the entries of all switched-on dictionaries for a lemma key.
components.detail: `entriesFor(key, lang)` reads the key's bucket in each shown dictionary of that language and returns matching entries in order, plus morphology cross-references (`#m`); `entryByRef` fetches one entry by key and id. Used by the dictionary pane and the map.

components.name: Installing dictionary packages
components.desc: Installs, registers and removes dictionary and morphology packages (*.gdpkg.gz) on the device.
components.detail: A package is gzipped JSON from the greekdict toolkit (`greekdict-pkg-2`); dictionaries and Greek morphology are stored as buckets in their own database, the Latin engine as one record, the small hints package in settings. Downloading is done by Instruments (dialogs.js); this code only reads files and writes them into storage.
components.netNote: receives packages that Instruments has downloaded or that you picked

mem: streamed install (v348): measured ~35–55 MB at peak; the Library still reads its (small) works whole with `readPackage`
store: all installed dictionaries, est. ~300 MB for the free set
cpu: unpacking, parsing and writing during install (seconds to ~25 s)

components.name: Reading a package file
components.desc: Unpacks a .gz file and parses its JSON.
components.detail: `readPackage` checks for the gzip header and pipes the file through `DecompressionStream`, reads the whole text, records its length as the size on the device and returns `JSON.parse` of it. Used for the Library's gzipped works (small); dictionaries are streamed instead (`scanPackage`, v348).

mem: the whole unpacked JSON of one work (median ~0.1 MB, largest ~9.5 MB)

components.name: Writing a package
components.desc: Stores a parsed package in its dictionary database without ever leaving the dictionary missing.
components.detail: `importPackage` handles three kinds: the Latin engine (`latmorph`, one `engine` record), the hints (`morphhints`: preferred lemmata and word classes into settings) and bucketed dictionaries/morphology, written 300 buckets per transaction with progress, then the headword list (`#hw`) for search, then stale buckets deleted. It records the package in the `dicts` store (name, source, licence, version, size). `bulkPut` writes main-database stores in chunks of 2,000 (used by the migration and backups). Since v348 a package is read as it streams in (`scanPackage`): unpacked bit by bit, split at its top level, each bucket parsed alone and stored in batches of 300 – never the whole package in memory (measured in Chrome: Greek morphology peak ~45 MB instead of ~1,040 MB; LSJ ~35 MB instead of ~98 MB).

mem: measured in Chrome: ~35–55 MB at peak while installing (streamed, v348); before: up to ~1 GB for Greek morphology
store: all installed dictionaries, est. ~300 MB for the free set
cpu: unpacking, parsing bucket by bucket and IndexedDB writes: ~22 s for Greek morphology, ~8 s for LSJ (desktop Chrome)

components.name: Installed dictionaries
components.desc: Knows which dictionaries and analysis tools are installed, switched on and in which order.
components.detail: `loadDicts` reads the `dicts` store, sorts the dictionaries by your order (`dictPrefs`), sets `S.shown`, chooses the Greek morphology, hints and Latin engine in use, and loads word classes and lemma preferences. `deleteDict` drops a dictionary's database and its record (and, for the hints, their settings).

components.name: Grammar line
components.desc: The small line under each word with its grammatical form, e.g. "masc/neut gen sg", configurable per word class.
components.detail: The text comes from the chosen analysis, compressed when several readings differ in only one feature; indeclinable words show their word class. Which word classes show the line is a setting (`gramCfg`), applied by an injected style sheet so no redraw is needed.

components.name: Grammar line text
components.desc: Turns analyses into the short line shown under a word.
components.detail: `gramText` strips dialect and clitic notes, and if several analyses differ in one position only, joins them ("nom/voc/abl sg"); otherwise it shows the first and "(+n)". `indeclClass` names the class of words that do not inflect, preferring the treebank's class for this passage (`CTX_POS`), then the analysis (`INDECL_RE`), then the lemma's usual class (`INDECL_LAB`), and handles Latin enclitics ("indecl + -que").

components.name: Which classes show it
components.desc: Chooses for which word classes the grammar line is shown.
components.detail: `GRAM_GROUPS` sorts the classes into Inflected words, Verb forms and Indeclinable and other; `GRAM_DEF` / `defaultGramCfg` show all but numerals, conjunctions, particles and other; `allGramCfg` shows all. `applyGramCfg` writes a `<style id="gramStyle">` that hides the line for switched-off classes.

components.name: Grammar line buttons
components.desc: The word-class buttons in Settings → Grammar line.
components.detail: `gramRowsHTML` builds the grouped buttons, `syncGramRows` updates their pressed state; `gramDialog`, an older stand-alone dialog, is not called anywhere now.

components.name: Word-class colours
components.desc: Colours each word by its word class (noun, verb, participle, particle …), with colours you can change.
components.detail: Fifteen classes with default colours (`POS`); the class of each word comes from its reading, treebank hints and the lemma. Colours are applied by an injected style sheet keyed on the `p-<class>` class of each word, so changing a colour needs no redraw.

components.name: Word classes
components.desc: The list of word classes with their names and default colours.
components.detail: `POS` holds id, label and default colour for 15 classes (incl. punctuation marks); `posLab` gives a label, `posOnOf` whether a class is coloured.

components.name: Finding the word class
components.desc: Decides the word class of a word from its lemma and reading.
components.detail: `posOf` checks the article and a list of Greek `PARTICLES`, then the analysis (participle, infinitive, finite verb), capitalised lemmas (proper nouns), the treebank class of the lemma (`S.lemmapos` / Latin `S.latPos`, mapped by `UPOS2`), indeclinable tags and finally case endings.

components.name: Applying the colours
components.desc: Switches the colouring on or off and applies the chosen colours.
components.detail: `applyPosColors` writes `<style id="posStyle">` with one rule per coloured class (and punctuation), toggles `body.pos` and the Colours button.

components.name: Colour buttons
components.desc: The buttons in Settings → Colourisation that switch classes and show their colours.
components.detail: `COL_GROUPS` adds punctuation to the grammar groups; `chipGroupsHTML` builds the grouped buttons for both the colour and the grammar settings; `syncPosRows` updates their state and colours. Holding a button opens the palette (in `wire`).

opens / deletes one database per dictionary
copies old buckets, 200 at a time
keeps the reading position on resize
rebuilds the map style for the theme

opens the text of a place or saved map
text, glosses by textId, marker, position

textRoot: full copy of the text
morphology buckets for the next 1,500 words
